Z523 was originally designed without a synchronous facilitation activity; therefore, the Multicultural Perspective Paper currently serves as the Z523 anchor assignment for Competency 6. The original course developer has recommended that this be reconsidered. Earlier discussions among the 523/Z523 course instructors recommended Group Facilitation as the anchor assignment, consistent with the facilitation-based anchor used in SW524. At the time Z523 was developed, a comparable facilitation activity was not included because of uncertainty about how it could be implemented in an asynchronous course. With students now able to meet and facilitate groups via Zoom, this limitation may no longer apply.
issues.recommendation: Flag Z523 for a future course redesign to consider replacing the Multicultural Perspective Paper as the anchor with an applied Group Facilitation assignment, aligned with the intended SW523 curriculum and adapted for the exclusively online format.

standards.title: Consistent graded-activity naming
standards.rationale: Use predictable names so learners can distinguish assignments, discussions, and graded discussions across the program.
standards.example: Use “Discussion Assignment” for graded discussions and reserve “Discussion” for ungraded interaction.

standards.title: Consistent rubric location
standards.rationale: Make grading expectations easy to find without duplicating generic material throughout a course.
standards.example: Use a standard Rubrics area and link the applicable rubric from each graded activity.

standards.title: Consistent Assignment and Discussion Deadlines
standards.rationale: Consistent weekly deadlines reduce cognitive load and help learners balance coursework with work, family, and other responsibilities. From a design perspective, a predictable rhythm simplifies course navigation, calendar planning, reminders, and instructor communication. Assignments should be due Sundays at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time, while initial discussion posts requiring peer responses should be due Thursdays at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time. This gives learners sufficient time to engage meaningfully with classmates before the week closes.
standards.example:
In a weekly module containing a discussion and written assignment:

Initial discussion post due Thursday at 11:59 p.m. ET
Peer responses due Sunday at 11:59 p.m. ET
Written assignment due Sunday at 11:59 p.m. ET

These deadlines are entered consistently in Brightspace and clearly stated in the syllabus, course calendar, weekly overview, and activity instructions. Exceptions are used only when necessary and communicated well in advance.

Note: “Eastern Time” or “ET” is preferable to “EST” because it remains accurate during both standard time and daylight saving time.
